title: Chiplever: Towards Effortless Extension of Chiplet-based System for FHE
problem: Chiplet-based systems with specialized accelerators lack native support for FHE polynomial operations. Current design approaches require building entirely new dedicated accelerators, causing repeated customization and inefficient resource utilization.
motivation: FHE is a critical privacy-preserving cryptographic technique with ideal security properties, but chiplet-based systems cannot efficiently support its computational demands without better resource utilization.
method: Chiplever proposes an extension framework that leverages existing abundant accelerator resources in chiplet systems rather than designing new ones. The approach enables polynomial operation support for FHE through compiler-based extension mechanisms and reuse of heterogeneous accelerators in the chiplet package.
key_novelty: Reusing and extending existing heterogeneous accelerator resources in chiplet systems to support FHE operations rather than designing new dedicated accelerators from scratch.
contributions: Proposes Chiplever framework for effortless FHE support in existing chiplet-based systems
Eliminates redundant accelerator design by leveraging existing system resources
Enables polynomial operation support for FHE through system extension mechanisms
Reduces design complexity and resource waste in heterogeneous chiplet architectures
limitations: Specific design tradeoffs, scalability, and comparison with baseline approaches not discussed in abstract.
